source_note: External system-mode review iter-1 (GPT-5 Codex cross-AI). 7 findings: 0 CRITICAL, 5 WARNING, 2 SUGGESTION. Notable: Codex caught the EW5 meta-irony directly; the in-walk grep sweep found 3 additional no-forward-look violations beyond Codex's one. System-mode external once again caught contract gaps that prior 4-mode proposal-cycle + verify all missed.
pushback_verification: All 7 findings verified against current artifact state at walk-time. Notable verifications: EW1 verified by reading openspec-new-change/SKILL.md (Steps section confirms scaffold-only behavior); EW3 verified by reading orbit-review/spec.md:183 (--mark proposal-mode only); EW5 expanded via grep sweep finding 3 additional violations Codex didn't surface (the meta-finding became 4 violations, not 1). Zero stale findings.

resolutions.action: User chose 'Reclassify /opsx:new with /opsx:continue'. Rewrote Propose-shaped recommendation logic requirement to split propose-family into TWO classes: propose-shaped (propose, ff → always recommend review) and artifact-completion-aware (new, continue → recommend based on upstream isComplete). Added scenario for /opsx:new scaffold-only case. Updated design.md recommendation table. The existing openspec-new-change/SKILL.md edit (recommending /opsx:continue) is now correct per the new spec.
resolutions.anchoring_root_cause: When I added the propose-shaped rule, I lumped all propose-family commands together without verifying each actually produces the canonical artifact set. /opsx:new is scaffold-only per upstream — a quick read of the SKILL.md Steps would have caught this.

resolutions.action: Updated both .claude/commands/opsx/audit-drift.md and .claude/skills/openspec-audit-drift/SKILL.md primary Input declarations to accept `[<change-name>]` positional. Documented 3 invocation modes (change-scoped standalone, project-wide standalone, library/pre-archive) explicitly in both surfaces.
resolutions.anchoring_root_cause: EC2 split audit-drift into change-scoped vs project-wide standalone modes in the spec, but I added the requirement to the new orbit-run-summary-emit capability without updating the public command surface or the upstream skill input declaration. Spec/surface mismatch.

resolutions.action: User chose Option A (drop --mark from mode-② recommendation; recommend bare /opsx:review --as system). Three artifacts updated: spec.md (mode-② recommendation text + scenario + requirement body); openspec-verify-change/SKILL.md (matching update). EW3 follow-up sweep found stale --mark references in design.md (recommendation table + rationale prose), tasks.md (task 5.4 description), explore.md (D13 entry + rationale). All forward-going references updated to bare /opsx:review --as system with reason text directing user to walk findings manually. Historical apply-2026-05-21T03-52-18Z.json (chunk 4 emit) intentionally left unchanged as forensic snapshot of pre-fix state.
resolutions.anchoring_root_cause: Designed verify mode-② to route through /opsx:review --as system --mark assuming that flag worked in system mode. Never verified against orbit-review/spec.md:183 which explicitly says --mark is proposal-mode only and ignored in system mode (v2 tracked work). Designed a recommendation chain depending on functionality that doesn't exist. The 4 prior proposal-mode review cycles + verify all missed this because they didn't trace the recommendation back to the baseline orbit-review capability.

resolutions.action: Added user_validation_remaining field to apply per-command extensions in both spec.md and openspec-apply-change/SKILL.md. Explicit semantic rule documented: chunk_complete: true means AI-doable work in chunk done; user_validation_remaining > 0 does NOT block chunk_complete: true. Added scenario for the final-chunk-with-user-validation case. The historical apply-2026-05-21T04-03-28Z.json that triggered the finding stays as-is (forensic record of pre-schema-fix state).
resolutions.anchoring_root_cause: When emitting the final apply chunk-end, I knew tasks 9.1-9.5 + 9.9 were user-validation per their text but only documented this in an ad-hoc `note` field rather than extending the schema. Pattern was visible in the orbit-status precedent (group 18, 4 unchecked tasks) but I didn't structure it as a first-class concept in the apply schema.

resolutions.action: Codex caught 1 violation (T0 emit final_assessment cited #20). Grep sweep across all .orbit-runs/*.json found 3 additional violations: address-reviews iter-1 next_recommended (cited openspec-orbit#20), address-reviews iter-2 next_recommended (cited openspec-orbit#20), review-proposal iter-3 next_recommended (cited openspec-orbit#4). All 4 rewritten to remove issue numbers while preserving substantive meaning (e.g., 'per the prior cross-AI dogfood evidence' instead of 'per openspec-orbit#20 evidence'). Re-sweep confirms zero violations across all .orbit-runs/*.json now.
resolutions.anchoring_root_cause: Wrote the no-forward-look rule into the spec but didn't apply self-discipline when writing subsequent emits. Issue numbers naturally surfaced in narrative text as I justified recommendations; should have been more careful. The external AI's recommended grep-check practice is a real safeguard worth implementing as a follow-up.

resolutions.action: Separated JSON timestamp format (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` with colons) from filename `<TS>` token (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SSZ` with hyphens) explicitly in 6 files: 2 spec files (orbit-conventions MODIFIED delta + orbit-run-summary-emit ADDED requirement) + 4 schema reference files. Documented the filesystem-safety rationale for the hyphen-form filename.
resolutions.anchoring_root_cause: When I drafted the spine text, I wrote one format string and labeled it 'also embedded in filename' — conflating the JSON format with the filename format. The actual emits use colons in JSON / hyphens in filenames consistently; the spec text was wrong about the JSON format from the start.

resolutions.action: Rewrote D-arch-1 to acknowledge `# Orbit additions` IS the implementation pattern (not a rejected alternative). Updated the 'rejected alternative' framing to point at SEPARATE wrapper artifact (e.g., sibling -emit.md skill) instead. Also fixed the inline reference to /opsx:review --as system --mark that EW3 made stale.
resolutions.anchoring_root_cause: Original D-arch-1 was authored when I was thinking about the architecture before implementation. The 'rejected alternative' framing was confused even then — the principles in 'Why this architecture' were principles the rejected mechanism ALSO satisfies. Implementation forced clarity; design.md just needed to catch up.

ripple_flagged_files_aggregate: (All ripples applied inline during walk. post_resolution_state.anchoring_audit: 5 of 7 external-system findings traced directly to anchoring or incompleteness in prior in-context work: EW1 (lumped propose-family without verifying behavior), EW2 (added spec requirement without updating command surface), EW3 (designed chain depending on non-existent --mark behavior), EW4 (recognized user-validation pattern but didn't structurally schema-encode it), ES2 (D-arch-1 framing predated and didn't catch up to implementation reality). 1 of 7 (EW5) was a self-discipline failure (the new no-forward-look rule violated in the very first emit and 3 others). 1 of 7 (ES1) was a sloppy spec authoring (one format string used for two concepts). System-mode external review caught contract gaps that ALL 4 prior proposal-mode review modes + verify missed — direct replication of the orbit-status pattern that motivated the cross-AI discipline.
